claims.statement: Extending an original leaf by one pendant edge can change the fixed-rank favorable tagged family and its complete aggregate even when the same rank remains eligible before and after the operation.
claims.scope: Retained for the exact encoded 18-vertex tree and its 19-vertex extension at p=8, and for the stated conditional pendant-extension recurrences; it is not a universal assertion about every extension and is not a refutation or proof of the primary aggregate inequality.
claims.reason: retained: Independent exact replay confirms both trees have alpha=12 and x=6 and satisfy x+2<=p and 3p<2alpha+1 at p=8. Every current leaf passes the strict Delta_p(T-v)<0 selector, with original supports and leaf multiplicities retained. The complete sums are -4256 and -6267, and the favorable tags change when old leaf 10 ceases to be a leaf and new leaf 18 is added. The pendant and deletion-polynomial recurrences check on the pair. This verifies extension instability only; both sums remain negative and no universal sign result follows.

limitations: The replay covers only the specified tree pair and is not an exhaustive generation or census.
Both full selected sums are negative, so this evidence does not refute the primary inequality or establish a sign reversal.
The recurrences do not prove the eligibility guards or selector signs universally after extension and do not bound the recomputed complete sum.
